analysis.investment_thesis: Crizac is a financially clean business — zero debt, consistent 5-year earnings — but at P/B of 6.72 and a Graham Number of ~₹82 vs. a market price of ₹230, the investor is paying nearly 3x intrinsic value with no margin of safety whatsoever. Mr. Market is offering this at a speculative premium; the disciplined investor waits for a price that compensates for risk.
key_strengths: Zero debt and zero finance costs across all 5 years — the balance sheet is clean as a whistle
Five consecutive years of positive and growing earnings (Net Profit CAGR 64.3%), satisfying the minimum earnings track record
Asset-light model with strong OCF (₹187 Cr in 2025) converting nearly all earnings to cash
key_risks: Price far exceeds intrinsic value — Graham Number ≈ ₹82 (EPS ~₹8.74, BVPS ~₹34.3) vs. market price of ₹230, a 180% premium
P/B of 6.72 is more than 4x Graham's maximum threshold of 1.5x — paying heavily for goodwill that can evaporate
'Other Income' (₹35–53 Cr) represents 23–46% of reported net profit across years, inflating earnings quality and masking true operating power
red_flags: Recent IPO — sellers (promoters at 79.94%) and bankers set the price, not the market; buyer beware
P/B of 6.72 is categorically unacceptable under any Graham framework
No dividend history provided — no demonstrated cash return to shareholders
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Crizac's operating business is genuinely admirable by structural measures: zero borrowings across five years, expanding margins (operating margin 21.2%), ROCE of 48%, and unbroken profitability since 2021. These are the hallmarks of a well-run, capital-light franchise in international student recruitment. However, the business's quality is entirely irrelevant to the value investor if the price reflects all of it — and at ₹230, it reflects far more than the facts warrant.

The Graham Number, calculated from 2025 EPS of ~₹8.74 and BVPS of ~₹34.3, yields an intrinsic value ceiling of roughly ₹82. The stock trades at 2.8x that figure. P/E of 20.8x and P/B of 6.72x both breach Graham's strict quantitative thresholds. Furthermore, a meaningful portion of net profit derives from "Other Income" (₹35–53 Cr), which is not core operating earnings and depresses the reliability of the earnings figure used in valuation. This is precisely the type of speculative-premium IPO situation where the intelligent investor steps aside and waits — if the price ever approaches ₹80–90, a re-evaluation is warranted.
